output.summary: A flowering perennial of African origin, although truly wild populations are not known with certainty; it is often grown as an annual in temperate climates. Its white-to-yellow flowers often have a red or purple basal spot, while its many-seeded pods quickly become fibrous and woody. The immature pods are eaten raw, cooked or pickled and release characteristic slime when cooked.
output.edibilityNote: Immature pods are eaten raw, cooked or pickled; young leaves are edible, roasted seeds substitute for coffee, and seed oil is edible.
